source: CBSE Class 8 Maths Assessment v4, sheet Interventions
orderOfOperations: Optimising time, effort and money – the order of operations: (1) diagnose with the paper + one probe (10 min); (2) fix prerequisites before anything else; (3) use free, high-evidence methods (worked examples, retrieval, interleaving, spacing) – they cover 9 of 10 gap types at ₹0; (4) spend money only on a written gap list, and re-test to see if it worked (#426 recommendation effectiveness). Rank 1 = do first; Effort = what it demands of the student; Money = Free / Low / Paid.

items.name: Prerequisite mini-lesson (20 min) + 10 practice items
items.whatToDo: Use the prerequisite listed for the subtopic. Teach only that earlier skill with 2 worked examples, give 10 items on it, then return to the failed subtopic.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Use the Prerequisite Map line. Teach ONLY the prerequisite skill with 2 worked examples, then 10 items on it, then return to the failed subtopic.
items.evidence: Koedinger 2023: gaps are mostly prior knowledge, not rate; fixing the prerequisite restores the normal 2.5%/opportunity gain

items.name: Free video + NCERT exemplar for the earlier-class chapter
items.whatToDo: Free official video or open course for the earlier-grade chapter (NCERT/DIKSHA, Khan Academy, board-endorsed resources), then solve level-1 exemplar items; the teacher checks 5 of them.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: DIKSHA / NCERT official videos or Khan Academy India for the Class 6–7 chapter; solve exemplar Level 1 items; teacher checks 5 items.
items.evidence: Retrieval + worked examples; zero cost

items.name: Peer tutor (a classmate at L4/L5) for 2 sessions
items.whatToDo: Structured peer session with a classmate at L4/L5: the peer explains one worked example, the learner explains it back, then 5 items each from a teacher-provided list.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Structured: tutor explains one worked example, learner explains it back, then 5 items each. Teacher provides the item list.
items.evidence: Peer explanation benefits both; cheaper than tuition

items.name: Self-explanation on 3 worked examples
items.whatToDo: Learner reads a fully worked example and writes WHY each step is done, then a counter-example where the rule fails. Mark the explanations, not the answers.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Student reads a fully worked example and writes WHY each step is done, then a counter-example where the rule fails. Teacher marks the explanations, not answers.
items.evidence: Self-explanation effect (Chi); targets the 'why' the rote learner skipped

items.name: Concrete → picture → symbol re-teach
items.whatToDo: Re-teach with a concrete or visual model first (diagram, manipulative, simulation, timeline or flowchart as the subject suits), then the formal rule or symbol.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Re-teach with a physical/visual model first (area model for identities, number line for rationals, grid for squares), then the symbolic rule.
items.evidence: CRA sequence; removes the abstraction jump

items.name: Compare-and-contrast pair
items.whatToDo: Give two items that look alike but need different ideas. The learner must say what differs BEFORE solving.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Give two items that look alike but need different ideas (direct vs inverse proportion; SI vs CI). Student must say what differs BEFORE solving.
items.evidence: Contrasting cases build the discriminating concept

items.name: Faded worked examples (4 → 0 steps shown)
items.whatToDo: Item 1 fully worked; item 2 last step blank; item 3 last two steps blank; item 4 unaided. Same method, new values each time.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Item 1 fully worked; item 2 last step blank; item 3 last two steps blank; item 4 unaided. Same method, new numbers each time.
items.evidence: Fading reduces load while building the procedure (Renkl/Sweller)

items.name: Deliberate practice set: 12 items, 3 difficulty steps, immediate feedback
items.whatToDo: 12 items in 3 difficulty steps (4 at D1, 4 at D2, 4 at D3) from the wider bank, with feedback after each block; redo any block with an error.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: 4 items at D1, 4 at D2, 4 at D3 from the wider bank; check after each block; re-do any wrong block.
items.evidence: Practice with feedback is the 2.5%/opportunity engine

items.name: Step-checklist card
items.whatToDo: Learner writes the method as 3 to 5 numbered steps on a card and ticks them on every problem for a week.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Student writes the method as 3–5 numbered steps on a card and ticks them on every problem for a week.
items.evidence: Externalises the procedure until automated

items.name: Estimate-first rule
items.whatToDo: Before answering, write an estimate or expected form of the answer (size, sign, units, key term). Compare at the end. Applies to every application item for two weeks.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Before solving, write an estimate and the expected size/sign. Compare at the end. Applies to every C3 item for two weeks.
items.evidence: Cuts arithmetic slips; builds checking habit

items.name: Slow-down protocol on D1–D2 items
items.whatToDo: Timed practice is paused; reach 95% accuracy on D1 to D2 items before timed work resumes.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Timed practice is paused; accuracy target 95% on D1–D2 before any timed work resumes.
items.evidence: Accuracy before speed

items.name: Sleep / study-block hygiene check
items.whatToDo: If sleep is short or a phone is in the study block, fix that first via the parent form (M2). Support context only, never a score.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: If sleep < 8 h or phone in study block: fix that first (parent form M2). Support context only – never a score.
items.evidence: Attention errors track sleep and distraction

items.name: Interleaved mixed set (this + 2 earlier subtopics)
items.whatToDo: 12 items shuffled across this and 2 earlier subtopics so the learner must CHOOSE the method. Ask 'which method and why?' before solving.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: 12 items shuffled across 3 subtopics so the student must CHOOSE the method. Ask 'which method and why?' before solving.
items.evidence: Interleaving improves method selection and transfer (Rohrer)

items.name: Context-swap items
items.whatToDo: Same method in 3 unfamiliar settings (everyday, another subject, current affairs). Use the C3-D4 items of the wider bank.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Same method in 3 unfamiliar settings (sports, shopping, science). Use the C3-D4 items of the wider bank.
items.evidence: Varied surface features → deep-structure schema (Perkins & Salomon)

items.name: Student writes ONE C4 item and its solution
items.whatToDo: Learner writes ONE item that combines two ideas, with its solution. The teacher or tutor solves it with the class.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Creating a two-idea problem forces the combination. Teacher solves it in class.
items.evidence: Generation effect; highest transfer per minute

items.name: Spaced retrieval schedule: day 1, 3, 7, 21
items.whatToDo: 3 to 4 retrieval-probe items on each date, closed book, self-marked. Dates go into the planner (M15).
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: 3–4 retrieval-probe items each time, closed book, self-marked. Put the dates in the planner (M15).
items.evidence: Spacing + testing effect; cheapest index to move

items.name: Error-log re-do
items.whatToDo: Every wrong item goes into an error log with the correct reasoning and is re-attempted after 7 days without looking.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Every wrong item copied into an error log with the correct reasoning; re-attempted after 7 days without looking.
items.evidence: Errorful retrieval strengthens the correct trace

items.name: Cumulative 10-minute weekly quiz
items.whatToDo: 5 items from earlier chapters every week; no marks recorded, just tallies.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Teacher gives 5 items from earlier chapters every week; no marks recorded, just tallies.
items.evidence: Keeps the whole year within the retention window

items.name: Restate-then-solve
items.whatToDo: Learner rewrites each word or source-based question as a one-line 'given / find' in own words (home language allowed) before answering.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Student rewrites each word problem as a one-line 'given / find' in own words (home language allowed) before any maths.
items.evidence: Separates reading load from maths load

items.name: Bilingual maths glossary (30 terms per chapter)
items.whatToDo: Bilingual glossary of about 30 key terms and phrases per chapter, each with an example. Built once, reused all year.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: 'Increased by / to', 'per', 'exceeds', 'consecutive', 'ratio of A to B' … with an example each. Built once, reused all year.
items.evidence: Most Class 8 word-problem errors are 10–15 recurring phrases

items.name: Paired reading of 5 word problems per week
items.whatToDo: Learner reads 5 questions aloud to a partner who paraphrases them; then swap.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Reads aloud to a partner who paraphrases; swap.
items.evidence: Fluency in the language of maths

items.name: Untimed re-test, then timed drills only after 90% accuracy
items.whatToDo: Prove competence untimed; then build speed with 5-item timed sets, adding one item per week.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Prove competence untimed; then build speed with 5-item timed sets, adding one item per week.
items.evidence: Speed should follow accuracy; removes anxiety confound

items.name: Time-budgeting card
items.whatToDo: Marks-per-minute guide on the paper and a 'skip and return' rule, practised on 3 mock papers.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Marks-per-minute guide on the paper; 'skip and return' rule practised on 3 mocks.
items.evidence: Test-taking strategy, not content

items.name: Brief anxiety protocol (if #111 high)
items.whatToDo: Two-minute breathing routine before tests; counsellor check-in if screened anxiety is elevated (T3, support only).
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Two-minute breathing before tests; counsellor check-in if screened anxiety is elevated (T3 – support only).
items.evidence: Anxiety, not ability, drives the untimed–timed gap

items.name: Predict-then-check on every quiz
items.whatToDo: Learner writes the expected score before marking; show the predicted-versus-actual trend weekly.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Student writes expected score before marking; teacher shows the gap trend weekly.
items.evidence: Calibration improves with feedback on predictions (Dunlosky)

items.name: Confidence tagging (already on Student Paper)
items.whatToDo: Use the 1 to 5 confidence rating on every item; review only the 'confident and wrong' items together.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Use the 1–5 column; review only the 'confident and wrong' items together – these are the real misconceptions.
items.evidence: Targets high-confidence errors first

items.name: Show evidence of success (under-confident students)
items.whatToDo: Keep a 'solved without help' list and look at it before tests.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Keep a 'solved without help' list; refer to it before tests.
items.evidence: Self-efficacy from mastery experiences (Bandura)

items.name: Shorten and schedule: 20-minute blocks, 5 days, one subtopic
items.whatToDo: Fixed time, fixed place, one goal: 20-minute blocks on 5 days, one subtopic. A planner event each day (M15); the parent only asks 'did you do the 20 minutes?'
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Fixed time, fixed place, one goal; planner event each day (M15). Parent only asks 'did you do the 20 minutes?'
items.evidence: Implementation intentions beat motivation

items.name: Choice + quick win
items.whatToDo: Learner picks which of 2 subtopics to start; the first task is at D1 so success comes within 5 minutes.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Student picks which of 2 subtopics to start; first task is at D1 so success comes in 5 minutes.
items.evidence: Autonomy and early success restart engagement

items.name: Trusted-adult check-in / counsellor referral if burnout signals
items.whatToDo: If burnout or social difficulty is flagged, route to the counsellor (M3) before any academic push.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: If #114 burnout or #170 social difficulty is flagged, route to counsellor (M3) before any academic push.
items.evidence: Wellbeing gates learning; T3 data never used for scoring

items.name: Paid tuition – only when gaps span 2+ chapters and the free plan has failed for 3 weeks
items.whatToDo: Buy targeted sessions (2 a week for 4 weeks) with a written list of the diagnosed gaps; re-test with the same paper after 4 weeks.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Buy targeted sessions (2/week, 4 weeks) with a written list of the diagnosed gaps; re-test with this paper after 4 weeks.
items.evidence: Money spent AFTER diagnosis is 3–5× more effective than blanket coaching

items.name: Adaptive practice app (low-cost)
items.whatToDo: Only if device and internet are adequate; use it for practice sets and spaced retrieval, not for teaching.
items.exampleCbseG8Maths: Only if #193 device/internet is adequate; use for the practice sets and spaced retrieval, not for teaching.
items.evidence: Automates spacing and feedback
